The metric dimension of a graph is the minimum number of vertices needed to uniquely identify all other vertices in the graph based on their distances to these vertices. In this paper, we introduce a new concept called the truncated metric dimension, which is the minimum number of vertices needed to uniquely identify all other vertices in the graph based on their distances to these vertices, but with a limit on the maximum distance considered. We provide a formula for the truncated metric dimension of a graph and use it to determine the truncated metric dimension of several types of graphs, including paths, cycles, complete graphs, complete bipartite graphs, and hypercubes. We also prove that the truncated metric dimension of a graph is equal to the metric dimension of the graph if the maximum distance considered is equal to the diameter of the graph.
